entries.answer: David is a Computer Science Ph.D. candidate at Northwestern University, advised by Peter Dinda.
David earned a B.S. in Computer Engineering from Clemson University (2019–2022) and is pursuing a Ph.D. in Computer Science at Northwestern University (2023–present).

David studies distributed heterogeneous computing, especially ways to make emerging accelerators practical for scientific workloads. His current work explores scheduling across distributed heterogeneous systems.
David began his research at Clemson in collaboration with Argonne National Laboratory, developing statistical methods to predict error-bounded lossy compression ratios for scientific data.
David works with the Legion runtime and Julia to run array-oriented scientific applications across distributed systems and NVIDIA GPUs as part of the Constellation project.
David researches Processing-in-Memory accelerators and uses Legion to reduce the programming and portability burden of adopting PIM systems.
David collaborates with Pat McCormick at Los Alamos National Laboratory on scheduling for distributed heterogeneous systems.
David is a recipient of the U.S. Department of Energy Computational Science Graduate Fellowship (DOE CSGF).
David is based in Chicago. You can reach him at david@krasow.dev or run `open contact.vcf` to save his contact card.
